headline: Light rain tonight, then stormy Friday and Saturday night with gusty south winds; more wet weather likely next week, details uncertain.
summary: As of Wednesday evening, a weak front is crossing western Washington with light rain tonight. Totals are small: under 0.25 inch for the interior lowlands and 0.25 to 0.50 inch on the coast. Rain should break into showers overnight, and Thursday morning turns drier. A stronger system arrives early Friday with steadier rain and increasing south winds. The heaviest rain falls in the Cascades and on the Olympic Peninsula. Winds should be strongest along the northern coast and from Whidbey Island northward, where forecasters see a 50 to 90% chance of gusts over 40 MPH. Elsewhere, gusts of 20 to 30 MPH are expected, especially near the water. Forecasters are still watching whether a Wind Advisory will be needed Friday, and none has been issued. Rain continues at times Friday night as a warm front lifts north, and Saturday turns warmer, with highs in the 60s for most areas. A cold front then brings more steady rain and gusty winds Saturday night into Sunday, with gusts of 20 to 35 MPH possible across more of the region. Snow levels (the elevation where rain turns to snow) fall from around 8000 feet Saturday to 4000-5000 feet by later Sunday, so the Cascades and Olympics get snow at higher elevations. High surf is possible on the coast Sunday and is being monitored. Sunday night into Monday is briefly drier. Next week could bring a longer stretch of rain, but forecast models disagree on whether the main band of moisture hits western Washington or stays farther north in British Columbia. No river flooding is expected in the next seven days, but repeated rain will soak the ground and raise river flows, which could become a concern with later storms. No land-based watches, warnings, or advisories are in effect. Gale Watches (for boaters) cover Thursday night through Friday afternoon on the east Strait of Juan de Fuca, the Northern Inland Waters including the San Juan Islands, and the coastal waters.
changes: Earlier discussions emphasized a Thursday night to Friday storm, with a low chance of strong winds and widespread rain totals. By afternoon and evening, the focus shifted to Friday winds, with a 50 to 90% chance of gusts over 40 MPH on the northern coast and from Whidbey Island northward. Forecasters also added a second storm Saturday night into Sunday, with snow levels falling, and uncertainty about next week.
